items.passage: Mangoes, mostly, though the orchard outside Surabaya had long ago given up deciding. Arisa counted eleven trees still standing and two that had lain down sometime before the rains. Thuy said the fallen ones were resting. Arisa said they were firewood with good manners. They walked the rows the way they had as girls, kicking husks, naming the trees after teachers they had disliked. At the gate Arisa took a parcel from her bag: the brass bell Thuy had mailed to her new flat in Jakarta, still in its paper, the knot untouched. Thuy looked at the knot, not at the bell. She did not ask why. Arisa tied the parcel to the lowest branch of the eleventh tree, where the wind could reach it, and stepped back. They waited. When it rang once, faintly, Thuy reached up and tightened the knot so it would hold through the season.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Teasing and tender toward a bond that has outlasted distance
Teasing and carefree toward an orchard left to fall apart
Teasing and guarded toward a gift that has caused offense
Teasing and tender toward every place from their girlhood
items.explanation: 앞부분의 '쉬는 중'·'예의 바른 땔감' 같은 농담과 건조한 나무 세기는 장난스러운 겉 어조를 만든다. 중간에 Arisa가 선물을 풀지도 않은 채 돌려주지만 Thuy가 이유를 묻지 않고, 끝에서 두 사람이 종을 둘만의 과수원 나무에 매달고 매듭을 단단히 묶는 동작은 거절이 아니라 함께한 장소에 우정을 남기는 다정함을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 겉 어조만 포착했고, C는 돌려준 선물을 불쾌감의 원인으로 뒤집어 읽었으며, D는 다정함의 대상을 어린 시절의 모든 장소로 넓혔다.

items.passage: Three rules for the salt pans, Aoife had told the squad on the first morning: hats on, water every hour, no running where the crust is thin. Lanying had broken the third rule once, two years ago today, and had not played a full match since. Now she sat on the cooler with her knee strapped, timing the others' sprints with a stopwatch that ran four seconds slow. Aoife did not correct it. She read the numbers aloud as given and wrote them on her clipboard in neat columns. At noon the team left for lunch in the van. Aoife stayed. She walked out to the thin place, where the white crust had split into plates, and stood there with her hands in her pockets. Lanying came after a while, limping, and stood beside her. Neither of them mentioned the date. Aoife handed her the clipboard and the pen, and Lanying wrote one more line at the bottom of the column, below the others, in her own hand.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Brisk and businesslike toward an ordinary day of training
Brisk and quietly solemn toward a loss both women still carry
Brisk and quietly relieved toward a loss now safely behind them
Brisk and quietly solemn toward the history of the whole squad
items.explanation: 앞부분의 규칙 나열과 기록을 적는 절차적 문장은 사무적인 겉 어조를 만든다. 그러나 오늘이 2년 전 Lanying이 규칙을 어긴 날이라는 정보, 팀이 떠난 뒤 Aoife가 홀로 갈라진 지점에 서 있는 모습, 날짜를 말하지 않은 채 Lanying에게 기록판을 건네는 끝 동작은 두 사람이 함께 품은 상실을 조용히 기리는 엄숙함을 드러낸다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 겉 어조만 잡았고, C는 침묵의 원인을 안도로 뒤집었으며, D는 대상을 팀 전체의 역사로 넓혔다.

items.passage: Chalk dust still lives in the grooves of the piano lid in Room 4, and I traced it with one finger while Thandiwe tuned the violin I had left behind twenty years ago. She remembered the winter concert one way: I had played the solo, she said, and stumbled, and kept going. I remembered it another way. I had not played at all; I had stood in the wings while a boy from the upper class played it in my place. We went over the details like clerks. The program, the coat rack, the radiator that knocked. She was certain about the radiator. So was I. Then she took a folder from the cabinet, the old programs, and found that winter's sheet. She looked at it for longer than reading takes. She closed the folder, slid it back behind the others, and asked me, Hala, to play the solo now, while the room was empty.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Methodical and detached toward a dispute over plain facts
Methodical and quietly embarrassed toward a mistaken memory
Methodical and quietly gentle toward an old disappointment
Methodical and quietly gentle toward all of her former pupils
items.explanation: 프로그램·옷걸이·라디에이터를 하나씩 대조하는 장면은 서류를 맞추듯 꼼꼼하고 건조한 겉 어조를 만든다. 그러나 Thandiwe가 기록을 읽는 데 필요한 시간보다 오래 들여다본 뒤 아무 말 없이 폴더를 다시 넣고, 빈 교실에서 지금 그 독주를 연주해 보라고 청하는 끝 동작은 무대에 서지 못했던 제자의 오래된 실망을 감싸 주는 다정함을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 겉 어조만 포착했고, B는 침묵의 원인을 교사 자신의 민망함으로 뒤집었으며, D는 대상을 모든 제자로 넓혔다.

items.passage: By six the boarding-house kitchen in Manila smelled of garlic rice, and Tyrese was already at the long table with the ledger open. 'Maestro,' he said when Ruoxi came down, and stood, as he did at rehearsals. Ruoxi waved him back into his chair. The house had been her mother's; the orchestra paid Tyrese a stipend that rarely reached the end of a month, and his rent here was, on paper, three months overdue. Ruoxi poured two cups of coffee and set the sugared one in front of him. He turned the ledger toward her. A column of small payments ran down the margin in his hand, each dated, each initialed: the plumber in January, the gas man, the property tax in March. Ruoxi read them twice. Then she took her own pen, struck through the line that said his rent was owing, and pushed the ledger back across the table. Tyrese closed it and went to wash the pans.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Ruoxi and Tyrese?
options: A junior player who defers to his conductor out of professional respect
A tenant who has fallen behind and depends on his landlord's patience
A landlord who forgives a debt to reward a tenant's tidy bookkeeping
A young musician who has quietly covered his mentor's expenses himself
items.explanation: Tyrese가 Ruoxi를 'Maestro'라 부르며 일어서는 앞부분은 공식적인 지휘자와 단원의 관계를 보여 주지만, 장부 여백에 그가 직접 적은 배관공·가스·재산세 지출은 그가 하숙집 운영비를 몰래 대 왔음을 드러낸다. Ruoxi가 그 목록을 두 번 읽고 밀린 월세 줄을 지우는 동작은 이 비용의 방향을 확인해 준다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 호칭이 말하는 공식 관계에 머물고, B는 도움의 방향을 뒤집었으며, C는 마지막 장면만으로 관계를 세워 지출 목록의 의미를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: I filled out the customs form in my grandfather's language while he watched, and Burak corrected my letters with the end of his pencil, tapping twice for every mistake. 'Again, Noor.' The post office at the edge of the village outside Cairo had one window and a clerk who knew him. Burak called him Effendi; the clerk called him Uncle. The parcel was for my mother in Izmir: his winter coat, two jars of honey, a photograph of the house. On the form there was a line for the sender's return address. I wrote ours. He took the pencil, crossed it out, and wrote the clerk's address instead, slowly, so I could copy the shapes later. Outside he gave me the receipt and the pencil both. That evening my mother called to ask when we were coming. He handed me the phone and went out to water the beans, and I answered in his language, carefully, the way he had taught me, that I would stay through the summer.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Noor and Burak?
options: A granddaughter who chooses to remain with a grandfather readying her departure
A strict tutor and a pupil whose lessons follow the rules of a classroom
A grandfather who quietly relies on his granddaughter to handle his errands
Two travelers who are working together to send their belongings back home
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Burak은 연필로 틀린 글자를 두 번씩 두드리며 'Again'이라고 말해 엄격한 교사처럼 보인다. 그러나 그가 코트와 집 사진을 딸에게 부치고 반송 주소를 집 대신 우체국 직원의 주소로 바꾸며 손녀가 나중에 따라 쓸 수 있게 천천히 쓰는 행동은, 자신이 남고 손녀를 떠나보낼 준비를 하고 있음을 보여 준다. 끝에서 Noor는 그가 가르친 언어로 여름 내내 머물겠다고 답해 그 계획에 조용히 맞선다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, B는 표면의 사제 관계, C는 의존 방향을 뒤집은 관계, D는 우체국 장면만 반영한 관계다.

items.passage: On Thursdays, after the courts closed, I carried Amelia's proofs down to the press room on Ogarna Street in Gdansk. She was retired by then and wrote small pamphlets on old cases. She insisted that I, Dmitri, address her as Judge, and she addressed me as Clerk, never by name. The pressman set her type; I read it back to her aloud. One week the pamphlet concerned a theft from the harbor office in a year I knew well, because my father had worked there. The draft named no one. Amelia listened to my reading without interrupting, as she always did, and at the paragraph describing the missing ledger she asked me to stop. She took the proof, removed one line with a ruler and a blade, and paid the pressman for a second setting from her own purse. The line had given the shift on which the ledger vanished. The following Thursday she called me Clerk, as before.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Amelia and Dmitri?
options: A retired judge who keeps a strict and formal distance from her assistant
A retired judge who quietly shields her assistant's family at her own cost
A young clerk who quietly guards his employer's reputation by editing her
A retired judge who grows wary of her assistant once his father comes up
items.explanation: Judge와 Clerk라는 호칭만 오가는 앞부분은 엄격하고 형식적인 거리를 보여 준다. 그러나 화자의 아버지가 일하던 항구 사무소 절도 사건 대목에서 Amelia가 낭독을 멈추게 하고, 장부가 사라진 근무조를 밝히는 한 줄을 잘라 낸 뒤 재조판 비용을 자기 돈으로 치르는 행동은 그녀가 조수의 가족을 조용히 보호하고 있음을 드러낸다. 다음 주에도 호칭을 바꾸지 않는 것은 그 보호를 드러내지 않으려는 태도와 이어진다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 호칭만 본 관계, C는 보호의 방향을 뒤집은 관계, D는 낭독을 멈춘 한 장면만 반영한 관계다.

items.passage: Four pans hung above the galley stove, and Joaquim's mother had ruled on each before Beatriz came aboard: the big one for beans, the small one for eggs, the copper one for show, and the black iron one for her alone. Beatriz learned the order in the first week. She scrubbed the iron pan when told, oiled it, and hung it back on its own hook at the far end, handle turned outward the way the older woman liked. In July the river ran high, and the boat stayed docked at Porto Alegre for a month while Joaquim worked the cargo cranes. His mother took to sitting on deck with her mending. One evening Beatriz, alone in the galley, cooked rice in the iron pan for the first time. She did not hide it. The next morning she found the pan washed and oiled already, hanging not on its old hook but on the one beside the stove, handle turned toward the spot where Beatriz stood to cook.
items.question: In the text, the black iron pan most likely represents which of the following?
options: The heavy daily chores that a cook must perform aboard a river boat
The strict rules by which the older woman keeps the bride at a distance
The place in the family that the older woman is now ready to open up
The strained bond between the women that the bride repairs by cooking
items.explanation: 처음에 쇠 팬은 시어머니만 쓰는 물건이고 Beatriz는 닦아서 먼 고리에 걸어 두기만 하므로, 부엌의 권한과 경계를 보여 준다. 그러나 Beatriz가 그 팬으로 밥을 지은 다음 날 시어머니가 팬을 씻어 화덕 옆 고리로 옮기고 손잡이를 Beatriz가 서는 쪽으로 돌려 둔 동작은, 그녀가 집안에서의 자리를 며느리에게 내주기로 마음을 바꾸었음을 보여 준다. 따라서 두 맥락을 모두 포괄하는 C가 정답이다. A는 팬의 문자적 기능, B는 앞 맥락만 반영한 의미이며, D는 마음을 바꾼 주체를 며느리 쪽으로 뒤집어 관계 회복으로 읽은 해석이다.

items.passage: Years later Zaynab could still describe the thing Consuelo gave her that winter: a tin whistle painted blue, the kind sold to tourists on the quay. Consuelo sold fish by day and swept the night pharmacy in Vigo where Zaynab's mother worked the late counter, and she had seen Zaynab practicing scales on a school recorder behind the till. The whistle was in the wrong key for every song Zaynab knew. She played it anyway, each night at ten, when Consuelo came in with her broom, and Consuelo leaned on the handle and nodded along until the tune was done. In March the old woman stopped coming; a nephew took over the broom. Zaynab kept the whistle in the drawer with the spare receipts. On the last night her mother worked there, Zaynab took it out, wiped it on her sleeve, and left it standing upright in the cup of pens beside the register, where the next clerk would find it.
items.question: In the text, the blue tin whistle most likely represents which of the following?
options: A cheap instrument that Zaynab uses to practice her musical scales
A mistaken gift that Zaynab endures to avoid hurting the old woman
A friendship that fades once the old woman stops visiting the shop
A nightly kindness that Zaynab chooses to pass along to a stranger
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 호루라기는 Zaynab이 아는 어떤 곡과도 조가 맞지 않는 '잘못된 선물'이지만, 그녀는 매일 밤 Consuelo 앞에서 그것을 불고 Consuelo는 끝까지 들어 준다. 즉 호루라기는 선물의 쓸모가 아니라 두 사람이 매일 주고받던 배려의 의식이 된다. 마지막에 Zaynab이 그것을 닦아 다음 직원이 볼 계산대 옆 컵에 세워 두는 동작은 그 배려를 낯선 사람에게 넘기는 행위이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 문자적 기능, B는 앞 맥락만 반영한 의미, C는 마지막 동작을 관계의 소멸로 뒤집어 읽은 해석이다.

items.passage: My father kept time by the lamp. At the Colombo station Shamsuddin wound the clockwork that turned the lens every four hours, and he wound it with a brass key he had borrowed from the keeper before him and, as far as anyone knew, never returned. I was eleven when I asked why he did not buy his own. He said this one fit. At sixteen I refused to learn the winding at all; I wanted engines, not lamps, and I told him so loudly. He wound the clock alone for three more years. When the station was automated, the men from the port authority asked for the key. He gave them a different one, from the drawer, which also fit. The morning I left for the engineering college in Kandy, he pressed the brass key into my palm and closed my fingers over it. I have it still, on a nail by my own door, and I, Hollis, wind nothing with it.
items.question: In the text, the brass key most likely represents which of the following?
options: A duty that is held in trust and handed down rather than kept
A tool that is needed to wind the clock that turns the lens
A debt that the father owes the old keeper and will not settle
A quarrel between father and son that ends with a final gift
items.explanation: 열쇠는 처음에 렌즈를 돌리는 태엽을 감는 도구이자 전임 관리인에게서 빌려 돌려주지 않은 물건으로 등장한다. 아버지는 당국에도 다른 열쇠를 내주며 그것을 지키고, 등대 일을 거부했던 아들이 떠나는 날 그 열쇠를 손에 쥐여 준다. 화자가 그것으로 아무것도 감지 않으면서도 문 옆에 걸어 두는 끝 동작은 열쇠가 소유물이 아니라 대를 이어 맡겨지는 책임임을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 문자적 기능, C는 '돌려주지 않았다'는 앞 맥락만 반영한 의미, D는 열쇠를 부자 갈등의 화해로 읽은 해석이다.

items.passage: Once, before the newspaper came, Itzel had swept Camila's barbershop in Oaxaca every Saturday for a few coins and a bottle of tamarind soda. Then her essay won the state prize, and her photograph went up in the window between the price list and the calendar. Customers asked her about scholarships. Camila asked nothing, but she stopped letting Itzel touch the broom; she handed her a magazine instead and pointed at the good chair by the mirror. Itzel sat in it every Saturday, turning pages she did not read, listening to the broom go around her feet. The prize had made her __a coat hung on the wrong peg__. In June she came early, before the shop opened, and found the broom behind the door. Camila, arriving, looked at the swept floor and said nothing, and set out two bottles of soda instead of one.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase suggests that the prize had made Itzel
options: admired by customers in a way that put her on display in the shop
burdened by new expectations that weighed on her during each visit
out of position in a setting where she once had a clear role
a forgotten item left behind by its owner in the barbershop
items.explanation: 비유 앞에서 Itzel은 수상 후 비질을 못 하게 되고 손님 자리에 앉혀지며, 읽지도 않는 잡지를 넘기며 자기 발 주변을 도는 빗자루 소리를 듣는다. 이 두 단서는 익숙한 공간에서 원래의 역할을 잃고 어울리지 않는 자리에 놓인 상태를 가리키며, 그녀가 스스로 다시 비질을 하자 Camila가 탄산음료를 두 병 내놓는 뒤 장면도 원래 자리를 되찾는 흐름과 맞는다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 전시·노출의 속성, B는 무게의 속성만 골랐고, D는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽은 해석이다.

items.passage: After midnight the barge went slow on the Clyde, and Rory and Eamon took turns at the bilge pump. Rory's hands had been bad since the winter; he wore two pairs of gloves and still dropped the handle sometimes. Eamon never mentioned it. He simply arrived ten minutes early each shift and pumped before the bell, so the water was already low when Rory came aboard. On paper they split the work evenly. In the log Eamon wrote Rory's initials beside his own hours. His help was __a lamp left burning in a room nobody entered__. Rory found the log one morning while looking for the tide tables. He read the column twice. That night he came twenty minutes early, and the pump handle was already wet, and the two of them stood beside it holding mugs of tea, neither one reaching for the handle.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase suggests that Eamon's help was
options: a source of warmth that eased the cold of the night shift
a wasteful effort that cost Eamon more than it gave Rory
a signal meant to guide Rory safely through his duties
a steady care offered with no wish to be noticed
items.explanation: 비유 앞에서 Eamon은 Rory의 손 문제를 한 번도 언급하지 않고, 일찍 와서 펌프질을 끝낸 뒤 일지에는 Rory의 이니셜을 자기 시간 옆에 적어 둔다. 이 두 단서는 아무도 보지 않는 곳에서 꾸준히 이어지는 배려를 가리키며, 이는 '아무도 들어오지 않는 방에 켜 둔 등'이라는 비유의 핵심 속성과 맞는다. 뒤에서 Rory가 일지를 발견하고 더 일찍 나오는 장면도 그 배려가 원래 드러나지 않도록 행해졌음을 전제한다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 온기, B는 낭비, C는 길잡이라는 다른 속성만 골랐다.

items.passage:
We rehearse in the customs shed at Tromso
because the hall is booked and the guard is kind.
Isadora tunes her cello to the hum of the heater.
Dongsik counts us in with his chin, never his voice.
Forty years of this. We do not discuss the tempo.

Trucks idle at the barrier; papers pass through a slot.
A man declares two crates of fish, a dog, a clock.
Between the second movement and the third
Dongsik lifts his bow and holds it there,
and Isadora waits, and the waiting is
__a passport stamped on both sides at once__,
then the bow comes down. The guard, half listening,
waves a truck through without checking its papers.
At the end she nods. He nods. Nobody claps.
Outside, the snow keeps its own count,
and the barrier rises for no one in particular.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase suggests that the pause in the music is
options: a silent agreement that each of them grants the other at once
an official delay that holds the music back like an inspection
a record of travel that marks how far the two friends have come
a travel document that allows the two musicians to cross over
items.explanation: 비유 앞에서 Dongsik은 목소리 없이 턱으로 박자를 세고, 두 사람은 40년 동안 템포를 말로 의논하지 않는다고 제시된다. 이 단서들은 말 없이 서로 동시에 허락을 주고받는 관계를 가리키며, 양쪽에 동시에 찍힌 도장이라는 비유가 바로 그 상호 승인을 나타낸다. 뒤에서 경비원이 서류 확인 없이 트럭을 통과시키는 장면도 문서보다 신뢰가 앞서는 분위기를 이어 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, B는 지연·검사의 속성, C는 기록·이력의 속성을 골랐고, D는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었다.

items.passage: Sequoia sent me her new manuscript in a box of cedar that her uncle had built, and for a week I thought the box was the gift. I am Chayton, her translator, and I had been working in the cellar of my mother's house on the plateau because it was the only cool room. Then the spring rain came through the north wall. I carried the pages upstairs in armfuls; the box stayed below, floating for two days. When she called, I apologized for the box. She was quiet. She said she had wanted me to keep the pages in it while I worked, and that her uncle had carved one word on the underside of the lid. I went down when the water fell. The cedar had swollen, and the word was __a footprint in mud that the rain had softened__. I could still read it. I translated it last.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase suggests that the carved word was
options: evidence that someone had walked through the cellar during the flood
a message that was blurred by the mishap but still came through
a sign that the box itself had been badly damaged by the water
a trace of the uncle's work that was slipping into the past
items.explanation: 비유 앞에서 화자는 상자 자체를 선물로 오해했고, 상자는 지하실 물에 이틀 동안 떠 있었으며, Sequoia는 상자 안쪽에 새겨진 한 단어에 뜻을 담았다고 말한다. 비가 '부드럽게 만든' 발자국이라는 비유는 형태가 흐려졌지만 남아 있는 흔적을 가리키고, 뒤에서 화자가 그 단어를 여전히 읽어 마지막으로 번역하는 장면이 이를 확인한다. 따라서 오해와 사고에도 뜻이 전해졌다는 B가 정답이다. A는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었고, C는 손상의 속성만, D는 시간에 따른 소멸의 속성만 골랐다.

items.passage: When the season ended, the cinema on Calle Feria in Seville showed one film a night to almost no one, and that was where Anselmo asked me to meet him. I, Lucia, was his interpreter for the move to Bergen: leases, bank forms, the school for his daughter. He brought the papers in a grocery bag. We sat in the ninth row with the house lights half up, and I translated each line in a low voice while the projectionist threaded the reel. Anselmo signed where I pointed. Between forms he watched the blank screen. My client was __an actor learning his lines in a language the audience had not yet arrived to hear__. When the film began, a Norwegian one with Spanish subtitles, he leaned forward and read the Norwegian words under his breath, half a second behind, and I stopped translating for him.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase suggests that Anselmo was
options: a performer anxious about facing a crowd of strangers in Norway
a man pretending to understand forms that he could not read
a man getting ready in advance for a life that had not yet begun
an actor rehearsing a script in an empty theater before a show
items.explanation: 비유 앞에서 Anselmo는 베르겐 이주를 위한 임대·은행·학교 서류에 하나씩 서명하고, 서류 사이사이 비어 있는 스크린을 바라본다. 이 두 단서는 아직 시작되지 않은 새 삶을 미리 준비하는 모습을 가리키며, 뒤에서 그가 노르웨이 말을 소리 죽여 따라 읽어 화자가 통역을 멈추는 장면도 그 준비가 이미 진행 중임을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 관객 앞의 긴장이라는 속성을, B는 연기를 '흉내'로 읽은 속성을 골랐고, D는 비유를 극장이라는 배경에 맞춰 문자 그대로 읽었다.

items.passage: Years ago Sigrid and Anneke had sung the same duet every night for a season, and since then they had not spoken. Now both worked the small vineyard outside Rotterdam at harvest, and Sigrid kept to the far rows. Each morning she left her full crates at the end of Anneke's row, where the cart stopped, then walked off before Anneke reached them. On the last day of picking, rain came early, and the two women ended up under the same shed. Anneke hummed the opening bars of the duet, softly, once. Sigrid's reply was ______. She sang the second line under her breath, and when Anneke turned toward her, she was looking out at the vines again, rubbing grape stain from her thumb.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: openly welcoming
politely reserved
tunefully nostalgic
tentatively receptive
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Sigrid는 말은 하지 않으면서도 매일 상자를 Anneke의 줄 끝에 두고 먼저 자리를 떠나, 거리를 두면서도 상대에게 다가가는 습관을 보인다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그녀는 노래의 다음 줄을 작게 이어 부르지만 Anneke가 돌아보자 다시 포도밭을 바라보므로, 응답은 하되 조심스럽고 망설이는 정도여야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 정도가 지나치게 적극적이고, B는 거리 두기라는 앞 습관만 맞을 뿐 노래로 응답한 점을 설명하지 못하며, C는 지문의 노래·과거라는 소재를 빌렸지만 뒤의 망설이는 동작과 맞물리지 않는다.

items.passage: Soren paid on time. For eleven years he had rented the room above Sunja's net shed at the Jeju harbor, and for eleven years he had paid with a handwritten slip listing every won, down to the coins. When the winch slipped in October and crushed a crate of her abalone, he was the one working it. The harbor office wanted a written account. Sunja offered to write it herself and say the cable had been old. Soren thanked her and took the form home. What he returned the next morning was ______. He had listed the cable's age and the weight of the crate, and, on a separate line in his small square hand, that he had looked away to light a cigarette.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: scrupulously candid
respectfully deferential
cautiously accurate
neatly businesslike
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Soren은 11년 동안 동전 단위까지 적은 쪽지로 월세를 내는 사람으로 그려져 꼼꼼함이 드러난다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그는 Sunja가 제안한 '낡은 케이블' 설명 대신 자신이 담배에 불을 붙이느라 한눈을 팔았다는 사실까지 따로 적었으므로, 자신에게 불리한 내용까지 숨기지 않는 정도의 솔직함이 필요하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 그가 감사 인사를 했다는 앞 장면만 반영하고, C는 정확하되 조심스럽다는 한 단계 약한 정도이며, D는 목록을 적는 습관을 빌렸지만 자기 잘못을 밝힌 핵심을 담지 못한다.

items.passage:
We meet on the promenade at four, Ofelia and I,
the board on the bench between us, the gulls on the rail.
Thirty years she has opened with the same pawn.
Thirty years I have answered it badly on purpose
so she can say, as she likes to say, Bartolo, you learn nothing.

This spring her hand shakes when she lifts the queen.
I do not look. I study the harbor, the cranes, a red ship.
Her move, when it comes, is ______,
and I answer as if it were the old one,
the same bad answer, the same small loss.
She says my line. I nod. The tide goes out
the way it has gone out every afternoon in Valparaiso,
and I set the pieces back for tomorrow.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: suddenly reckless
noticeably altered
carefully rehearsed
slowly deliberate
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 30년 동안 같은 첫수에 일부러 서툴게 응수해 왔고, 올봄 Ofelia의 손이 떨리는 것을 보지 않으려고 항구를 바라본다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그는 그녀의 수에 '옛날 수인 것처럼' 같은 엉터리 응수를 하므로, 그 수는 예전과 달라진 것이어야 하고 그는 아무것도 변하지 않은 척하고 있다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 변화의 성격을 무모함으로 과하게 읽었고, C는 반복이라는 소재를 빌렸지만 '옛날 수인 것처럼'과 맞지 않으며, D는 손 떨림이라는 앞 단서 하나만 반영한다.

items.passage: On Sundays Nicolas sold walnut sweets from a folding table outside the cemetery gate in Tbilisi, and on Sundays I, Vesna, bought two and asked for the recipe. He was a retired sailor and gave answers like weather reports: some sugar, the right walnuts, enough time. I wrote down whatever he said. The list never matched the one from the week before. Last winter he was ill, and his table stood empty for a month. When he came back, he pressed a paper bag into my hands that held no sweets, only walnuts, a jar of grape must, and a length of string. His instruction was ______. He stood beside me at my own stove that evening and guided my hands, and did not leave until the first strand had set.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: precisely written
vaguely poetic
wordlessly practical
sweetly nostalgic
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Nicolas는 레시피를 물을 때마다 날씨 예보처럼 모호한 말만 했고 그 목록은 매주 달랐으므로, 그는 말로 정확한 방법을 전하는 사람이 아니다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그는 재료를 건넨 뒤 화자의 부엌에서 직접 손을 이끌며 첫 가닥이 굳을 때까지 곁에 있었으므로, 가르침은 말이 아닌 실제 동작으로 이루어져야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 앞의 습관과 맞지 않고, B는 앞의 모호한 대답만 반영해 뒤의 직접 시범을 설명하지 못하며, D는 단 음식이라는 소재를 빌린 표현이다.

items.passage: When the snow closed the road above Naples, my mother, Esperanza, and I had three days in the cabin with her mother, Assunta, and the question we had driven up to ask. I was leaving for college in a week. My mother had brought brochures for a residence in the city; she left them on the table, in the bread basket, by the stove, and each time Assunta moved them, unread, to the windowsill. On the second night the power failed. Assunta lit the lamps herself and made soup in the dark without searching for anything. My mother watched her hands. Her answer, the next morning, was ______. She gathered the brochures from the sill, folded them into her coat pocket, and asked Assunta to show me how to bank the stove before we left.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: firmly insistent
openly defeated
warmly nostalgic
quietly relenting
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Esperanza는 안내 책자를 식탁·빵 바구니·난로 옆에 계속 놓아두며 어머니를 설득하려 하고, 정전된 밤 Assunta가 혼자 능숙하게 등을 켜고 수프를 끓이는 손을 지켜본다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그녀는 책자를 말없이 주머니에 넣고 Assunta에게 난로 관리법을 아들에게 가르쳐 달라고 부탁하므로, 계획을 조용히 거두는 반응이어야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 앞의 끈질긴 행동만 반영하고, B는 물러서는 방향은 맞지만 정도가 지나치며, C는 가족·오두막이라는 소재를 빌렸지만 책자를 거두는 행동과 맞물리지 않는다.

items.passage: Two iced coffees, condensed milk at the bottom, a paper straw already going soft: Arman ordered for both of them without asking, as he had every morning that month. The cafe at the Chiang Mai station faced platform two, and Kiet sat facing it too, his bag between his feet, the letter from the boarding school in Bangkok folded into quarters in his shirt pocket. Arman talked about the timetable. The 8:30 was usually late; the 9:10 had a better carriage; the seats on the left got the morning sun until Lampang. He described the vendors who would come through with sticky rice, and which ones to avoid. He described the toilets. Kiet said yes, thank you, he knew. Arman drank his coffee. When the 8:30 was announced, on time, he stood, picked up Kiet's bag before Kiet could reach it, carried it to the carriage door, handed it up, and stayed on the platform with his hands in his pockets until the train had passed the signal box.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From busy practicality to formal courtesy, as Arman keeps up appearances
From busy practicality to quiet withdrawal, as Arman regrets talking too much
From busy practicality to quiet resentment, as Arman resists Kiet's departure
From busy practicality to quiet support, as Arman accepts Kiet's choice to go
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Arman은 열차 시간표·좌석·노점·화장실까지 촘촘하게 설명하며 분주하고 실용적인 어조를 만든다. Kiet가 '알고 있다'고 정중히 답한 뒤 설명은 사라지고 문장도 짧아지며, Arman은 커피만 마신다. 끝에서 그가 Kiet보다 먼저 가방을 들어 객차 문까지 옮겨 주고 열차가 신호소를 지날 때까지 플랫폼에 서 있는 동작은 떠나기로 한 의붓아들의 선택을 받아들이고 지지하는 마음을 드러내므로 D가 정답이다. A는 유지된 겉 정중함만 보았고, B는 전환의 원인을 Arman 자신의 말에 대한 후회로 뒤집었으며, C는 조용한 전환의 성격을 반감으로 한 단계 달리 읽었다.
